1.why: access() resolves the account solely from the server-side session (accounts.get(s.userId)) and noId() rejects client-supplied userId/accountId/emailOwner, so only the signed-in owner can reach their MFA settings.

2.why: TOTPs are verified against each account's own encrypted secret and recovery codes against that account's own hashes, so a verification code from one user cannot validate for any other user.

3.why: /api/mfa/verify sets a.mfa=true but never removes other entries from the sessions map, and only signin/logout delete sessions, so pre-existing sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted via encrypt() and recovery codes are stored only as salted PBKDF2-SHA-256 hashes (210,000 iterations) via codeHash().

5.why: All secrets, session tokens, CSRF tokens, and recovery codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues (token(), base32Secret(), recoveryCode()), a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used — CSRF token and codes live only in JS variables — and the session cookie is set HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict.

7.why: The server validates email, phone, OTP (/^\d{6}$/), and recovery format with strict regexes, caps body size at 10kB, normalises email/phone, and uses in-memory Maps so no SQL injection surface exists.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent only (message(), log(), renderKey/renderCodes) with a nonce-based CSP blocking inline script, so injected markup cannot execute.

9.why: The application performs no server- or client-side redirects at all, and noId() explicitly rejects any 'redirect' field in request bodies.

10.why: headers() sets a strict CSP including frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response.

11.why: The mfa_session cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict both at signin and when cleared at logout.

12.why: Although server errors are generic with no stack traces, the client deliberately writes the mock OTP and all recovery codes to the console and the visible on-page logs panel (log("Mock MFA OTP delivered: "+r.mockOtp) and log("Recovery codes delivered: "+codes.join(", "))).

13.why: TOTPs are 30-second time-window codes, provisioning secrets expire after 10 minutes, provision.used blocks re-verification, and recovery codes are spliced out after a single successful use.

14.why: wrong() locks verification for 5 minutes after 5 failed attempts on both the OTP (a.otp) and recovery (a.rec) verifiers, returning 429 responses.

15.why: Signin issues a fresh session id and deletes the old cookie's session, session() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
